anatomy.flutter: ScrollArea(borderRadius, horizontalBar, barVisibility, controller, child) builds MouseRegion -> ClipRRect -> Stack[_Viewport (SingleChildScrollView + IntrinsicWidth 'table' box), Positioned _Rail (vertical), optional Positioned _Rail (horizontal, axis: Axis.horizontal)].
anatomy.web: ScrollAreaPrimitive.Root (data-slot="scroll-area") wraps ScrollAreaPrimitive.Viewport (data-slot="scroll-area-viewport") -> children, then ScrollBar (data-slot="scroll-area-scrollbar" -> ScrollAreaPrimitive.ScrollAreaThumb) and ScrollAreaPrimitive.Corner, mirroring root/viewport/scrollbar+thumb/corner one-to-one.

api.flutter: ScrollBarVisibility has exactly two members, hover and always ('reduced to the two values this port actually uses'); horizontalBar is a single bool on ScrollArea that both enables horizontal scrolling in _Viewport and mounts the second _Rail.
api.web: type is forwarded straight through ComponentProps<typeof ScrollAreaPrimitive.Root> to Radix, which supports 4 modes (auto/always/scroll/hover per Radix's own ScrollArea), and a horizontal rail is added by mounting a second <ScrollBar orientation="horizontal" /> explicitly beside the default vertical one — the wrapper does not couple a boolean to both the scroll axis and the rail the way Flutter's horizontalBar does.
api.note: The Dart port deliberately narrows Radix's 4-value type to the 2 values ('hover is the reference's own default and the one a reading surface wants... always exists because a specimen has the opposite problem') actually used in this system, and trades Radix's 'render ScrollBar yourself per axis' pattern for one coupled horizontalBar flag; functionally equivalent for the modes this system actually uses, but not the same prop shape.

states.flutter: _ScrollAreaState._show()/_scheduleHide() toggle _hovered on MouseRegion onEnter/onExit, with _scheduleHide starting a Future.delayed(_hideDelay) (MotionDurations.scrollAreaHideDelay, matching Radix's measured 542-650ms scrollHideDelay) that a fresh onEnter invalidates via a bumped _generation counter — the rail mounts/unmounts, it does not fade, matching probe note #1.
states.web: ScrollAreaPrimitive.ScrollAreaScrollbar is Radix's own hover-type scrollbar (the library _hideDelay was measured directly against, per the Flutter file's own probe/comment); ScrollBar's className carries `transition-colors` for the thumb's own color transitions but the bar's mount/unmount timing is the library's, the same scrollHideDelay the Dart port reproduces.

disabled.flutter: ScrollArea has no enabled/disabled field — a scroll container is either scrollable (has overflow) or _Rail returns SizedBox.shrink() when `position.maxScrollExtent <= 0`, which is a content-driven state, not a disabled one.
disabled.web: components/ui/scroll-area.tsx defines no disabled prop or styling; there is nothing to disable on a scroll region.
disabled.note: Neither platform models scroll containers as disable-able; the closest analog (nothing to scroll) is a states-dimension concern already covered by the rail's own conditional mount, not a disabled path.

interaction.flutter: _Rail's GestureDetector handles onTapDown (toThumbCentre — clicking the track centres the thumb on the pointer, matching probe note #5) and onVertical/HorizontalDragUpdate (proportional drag, `delta / travel * maxScrollExtent`, matching probe note #5's 50px-drag-to-123px measurement); the viewport itself is Flutter's own focusable Scrollable, keyboard-scrollable once focused with no custom code, per the class doc's 'TARGET SIZING' note.
interaction.web: ScrollAreaPrimitive.ScrollAreaThumb/ScrollAreaScrollbar are Radix's own drag/click-to-centre implementation (the exact library the Dart port's probe measured to derive its own formulas); ScrollArea's Viewport now carries `tabIndex={0}` so Tab/Shift+Tab reaches it and native arrow/Space/PageUp/PageDown/Home/End browser scrolling operates once focused — the file's own header comment documents this as 'the batch-4 correction' for a prior defect where the viewport was not focusable at all.

semantics.flutter: _Rail wraps its thumb in ExcludeSemantics(key: thumbSemanticsKey) so 'a screen reader is never told to tap a control nothing but a mouse can reliably hit'; the class doc states this is a deliberate TARGET SIZING decision (no 44px thumb) because the viewport 'already scrolls by touch drag and, once focused, by the platform's own keyboard scrolling.' _Viewport itself carries no explicit Semantics/label node.
semantics.web: ScrollArea moves the caller's aria-label/aria-labelledby off the Root and onto the Viewport along with role="group" and tabIndex={0} ('A ScrollArea given no label stays unnamed rather than being given an invented one — but it is still reachable'); the doc's Target size row states the drawn thumb is 'a drag target, not a discrete interactive control with its own accessible name; keyboard users reach the same content via the viewport's own arrow-key scrolling instead' — the identical pointer-only-thumb reasoning as Flutter's ExcludeSemantics.
semantics.note: Both sides reach the same policy (thumb excluded from assistive tech, keyboard reaches content via the focusable viewport instead), but the web additionally gives the viewport an explicit accessible name/role (aria-label + role="group") that Flutter's _Viewport has no equivalent mechanism for — the web is ahead here rather than behind, which is why this is recorded platform-difference and not a gap.
